title: Ram Emoji 🐏 Meaning: Aries, Team Spirit and Abraham's Ram
description: 🐏 is a male sheep with curled horns. See how the ram emoji is used for Aries, sports teams like the Rams, stubbornness, and the ram of Abraham in scripture.
summary: The 🐏 ram emoji shows a male sheep with heavy curled horns. It is used for Aries birthdays and horoscopes, for teams called the Rams, for headstrong determination, and for farm animals. In religious posts it recalls the ram Abraham sacrificed in place of Isaac and the shofar blown from a ram's horn.
meaning: Astrology is the biggest everyday use. The ram is the sign of Aries, roughly late March to mid-April, so 🐏 decorates birthday posts, horoscope memes and "Aries season" jokes about impatience and charging ahead. People born under the sign also add it to bios, and they pair it with ♈ or 🔥 to stress the sign's reputation for boldness.

Sports fans use it constantly. The NFL's Los Angeles Rams and many college teams, including Colorado State, Fordham, Rhode Island and VCU, are the Rams, so 🐏 works as a cheer, a score update or a fan bio marker. Outside sports, "ramming" through obstacles gives it a gym and hustle reading: stubborn, unstoppable effort.

The ram also has deep roots in scripture. In Genesis 22, God provides a ram caught in a thicket, which Abraham sacrifices in place of his son Isaac. Jews recall this at Rosh Hashanah, when the shofar, a ram's horn, is blown. Muslims commemorate the same story, with Ibrahim and his son, at Eid al-Adha, when a sheep or other animal is sacrificed. Christian writers have long read the ram as foreshadowing Christ's sacrifice.

Literal use covers sheep farms, bighorn sightings in the Rockies and wool. Unicode has separate emojis for the ram and the ewe, so 🐏 is specifically the male. Farmers and 4-H families post it at shearing time and county fairs, and hikers in the Rockies use it for bighorn sheep, whose curled horns the emoji resembles closely.

contexts.label: In astrology
contexts.body: Aries birthdays and horoscope accounts lean on 🐏 every spring. Memes about Aries being competitive, quick to anger and first to start anything use it as the sign's mascot. ♈ is the formal zodiac symbol; 🐏 is the friendlier, more playful version.

contexts.label: In sports
contexts.body: Fans of the Los Angeles Rams and the many college Rams fill game threads with 🐏, often next to team-color hearts. It appears in score updates, draft-day posts and bios. Rival fans occasionally use it mockingly, but usually it is pure support.

contexts.label: In faith and holidays
contexts.body: Around Rosh Hashanah, 🐏 can point to the shofar and the binding of Isaac. Muslim families sometimes use it in Eid al-Adha posts about the sacrifice. In Christian Bible study it illustrates Genesis 22, though the Lamb of God imagery uses the ewe or lamb emoji instead.

combos.meaning: Aries, the zodiac sign symbolized by the ram.
A pair of sheep, male and female, or a flock.
Aries energy or fiery, headstrong determination.

confusedWith.difference: 🐑 is the ewe, a female sheep with a fluffy coat and no big horns. It is the usual emoji for lambs, wool, counting sheep and the Lamb of God. 🐏 is the horned male.
🐐 is a goat, with straighter horns and often a beard. It is also the GOAT, greatest of all time, which 🐏 never means.
♈ is the abstract zodiac sign for Aries, drawn as stylized horns on a purple tile. 🐏 is the animal itself and works more casually.

avoid: Do not use 🐏 for "greatest of all time"; that is 🐐.
Avoid it for the Lamb of God or a newborn lamb, where 🐑 is the fitting choice.
design: A side view of a stocky sheep with thick, spiraled horns curling around the ears, usually with a cream or white woolly body. Some platforms draw a fluffier domestic ram and others something closer to a bighorn, with a smoother coat, but the curled horns are always the focus and are what tells it apart from the ewe.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 🐏 and 🐑?
faqs.a: 🐏 is the ram, a male sheep with large curled horns. 🐑 is the ewe, a female sheep without them. Use 🐑 for lambs, wool and counting sheep; use 🐏 for Aries, the Rams or toughness.
It is commonly used that way, since the ram is the animal of Aries. The official zodiac symbol is ♈, but many people prefer the animal because it is more recognizable and playful.

faqs.q: What does the ram mean in the Bible?
faqs.a: The best-known ram is in Genesis 22, provided by God as a sacrifice in place of Isaac. Rams also appear in temple offerings in the Law of Moses, and their horns were made into the shofar used in Jewish worship.
It almost always refers to a team called the Rams, most often the NFL's Los Angeles Rams, or one of several college Rams teams. Fans use it to cheer and to tag game posts.

faqs.q: When was the ram emoji added?
faqs.a: 🐏 is listed under Emoji 1.0, dated 2015, the first formal emoji version. It is supported on all major platforms, alongside 🐑 for the ewe and 🐐 for the goat.
